title: Sphingolipid Metabolic Pathway Impacts Thiazide Diuretics Blood Pressure Response: Insights From Genomics, Metabolomics, and Lipidomics.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
study_design: Prospective pharmacogenomic cohort analysis (PEAR) with cohort replication (PEAR blacks, GERA whites) and lipidomics sub-study
intervention: Hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy: PEAR 12.5 mg/day escalated to 25 mg/day over 9 weeks; replication GERA cohort received 25 mg/day for 4 weeks.
comparators: Genotypic groups within SPTLC3 (rs6078905) carriers vs noncarriers; atenolol-treated cohort used for specificity testing.
primary_outcome: Change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure after hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy.
secondary_findings: Replication analysis in PEAR blacks identified additional significant SNP signals within the SPTLC3 region associated with diastolic BP response.; No statistically significant replication was achieved in the GERA white cohort (office BP phenotype).; Baseline sphingomyelins (N24:2, N24:3, N16:1, N22:1) were higher among rs6078905 CC genotype carriers in lipidomics analyses.
conclusions: SPTLC3 genetic variation and sphingomyelin metabolism influence hydrochlorothiazide blood pressure response, supporting precision antihypertensive therapy.
authors: Shahin MH, Gong Y, Frye RF, Rotroff DM, Beitelshees AL, Baillie RA, Chapman AB, Gums JG, Turner ST, Boerwinkle E, Motsinger-Reif A, Fiehn O, Cooper-DeHoff RM, Han X, Kaddurah-Daouk R, Johnson JA
